# dlarfg

> Generate a real elementary reflector (Householder matrix).

<section class="intro">

A **Householder transformation** (or an **elementary reflector**) is a linear transformation that describes a reflection about a plane or a hyperplane containing the origin.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var dlarfg = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dlarfg' );
```

#### dlarfg( N, alpha, x, strideX )

Generates a real elementary reflector `H` such that

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:householder_transformation" align="center" raw="H \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ \mathbf{x} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \beta \\ \mathbf{0} \end{bmatrix}" alt="Householder transformation equation"> -->

```math
H \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ \mathbf{x} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \beta \\ \mathbf{0} \end{bmatrix}
```

<!-- <div class="equation" align="center" data-raw-text="H \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ \mathbf{x} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \beta \\ \mathbf{0} \end{bmatrix}" data-equation="eq:householder_transformation">
    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/stdlib-js/stdlib@develop/lib/node_modules/@stdlib/lapack/base/dlarfg/docs/img/equation_householder_transformation.svg" alt="Householder transformation equation">
    <br>
</div> -->

<!-- </equation> -->

where `H` is an `N`-by-`N` orthogonal matrix, `alpha` is a scalar, `x` is an `(N-1)`-element vector, and `beta` is a scalar. The matrix `H` is represented in the form

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:householder_matrix" align="center" raw="H = I - \tau \mathbf{v} \mathbf{v}^T" alt="Householder matrix representation"> -->

```math
H = I - \tau \mathbf{v} \mathbf{v}^T
```

<!-- <div class="equation" align="center" data-raw-text="H = I - \tau \mathbf{v} \mathbf{v}^T" data-equation="eq:householder_matrix">
    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/stdlib-js/stdlib@develop/lib/node_modules/@stdlib/lapack/base/dlarfg/docs/img/equation_householder_matrix.svg" alt="Householder matrix representation">
    <br>
</div> -->

<!-- </equation> -->

where `tau` is a scalar and `v` is an `N`-element vector with `v[0] = 1` and `v[1:N]` stored on exit in `x`.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );

var tau = dlarfg( 3, 4.0, x, 1 );
// tau => ~1.714...

// x now contains the vector v with v[0] implicitly being 1
// x => <Float64Array>[ ~-0.557..., ~-0.742..., ~-0.371... ]
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **N**: number of elements in the vector `v`.
-   **alpha**: scalar `alpha`.
-   **x**: input [`Float64Array`][mdn-float64array] containing the `(N-1)`-element vector `x`. On exit, contains the `(N-1)`-element vector `v[1:N]`.
-   **strideX**: stride length for `x`.

The function returns `tau`, the scalar factor of the elementary reflector.

Note that indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use [`typed array`][mdn-typed-array] views.

<!-- eslint-disable stdlib/capitalized-comments -->

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

// Initial array:
var x0 = new Float64Array( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );

// Create offset view:
var x1 = new Float64Array( x0.buffer, x0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 ); // start at 2nd element

var tau = dlarfg( 3, 4.0, x1, 1 );
// tau => ~1.714...

// x0 => <Float64Array>[ 0.0, ~-0.557..., ~-0.742..., ~-0.371... ]
```

#### dlarfg.ndarray( N, alpha, x, strideX, offsetX )

Generates a real elementary reflector using alternative indexing semantics.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );

var tau = dlarfg.ndarray( 3, 4.0, x, 1, 0 );
// tau => ~1.714...

// x => <Float64Array>[ ~-0.557..., ~-0.742..., ~-0.371... ]
```

The function has the following additional parameters:

-   **offsetX**: starting index for `x`.

While [`typed array`][mdn-typed-array] views mandate a view offset based on the underlying buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on a starting index. For example,

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var x = new Float64Array( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );

var tau = dlarfg.ndarray( 3, 4.0, x, 1, 1 );
// tau => ~1.714...

// x => <Float64Array>[ 0.0, ~-0.557..., ~-0.742..., ~-0.371... ]
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarfg()` corresponds to the [LAPACK][lapack] routine [`dlarfg`][lapack-dlarfg].
-   If `N = 1`, then `tau = 0` and `H` is the identity matrix.
-   The sign of `beta` is chosen so that `beta` has the opposite sign of `alpha` to avoid cancellation errors.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var dlarfg = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dlarfg' );

// Generate a random vector:
var x = uniform( 5, -10.0, 10.0, {
    'dtype': 'float64'
});
console.log( 'x: %s', x );

// Generate random alpha:
var alpha = uniform( 1, -10.0, 10.0, {
    'dtype': 'float64'
})[ 0 ];
console.log( 'alpha: %f', alpha );

// Generate the Householder reflector:
var tau = dlarfg( x.length, alpha, x, 1 );
console.log( 'tau: %f', tau );
console.log( 'v (stored in x): %s', x );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
